designed_from: the v1 discovery table (research/E4/CRYPTO/discovery/plans.csv, research/E4/REPORT.md); nothing from the validation period or the holdout was read. v2 is a second design on discovery data, declared as such; validation remains the single test and has not been touched
question: Under a realistic short model (isolated-margin liquidation at +100%, redenomination-sized jumps treated as non-trades) and with one pre-specified regime condition, does the fade on the short side earn a positive net return after fees, slippage and carry, beat matched random shorts under the same plan, win more often than it loses, keep its tail bounded, and do so in every discovery year?

changes_from_v1.short_model: liquidation: a short is liquidated at the first session whose high is 100% above the entry, losing the sold notional plus fees and carry (an isolated-margin perpetual at 1x; intraday spikes liquidate, as they do in reality). jump_ratio 10: a session whose close/reference ratio is beyond 10x or below 1/10 inside (entry, exit] is a redenomination or a bad print (COCOS 2021-01-16, 1000:1), and the trade is EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP for the rule and the baselines alike
changes_from_v1.regime: the four v1 detectors are joined by their _BEAR variants: the same flag only when BTC's close is below its 50-session mean at the signal close (idxsig/rules/moonshot_e4.py bear_regime; known at the decision; no signal when BTC or 50 sessions of it are missing). v1 found every plan negative in 2021 and nearly every plan positive in 2022; this is the one regime proxy pre-specified here, the most ordinary one, with no threshold search
changes_from_v1.tail_criterion: v1's 1st-percentile rule is unsatisfiable under liquidation by construction (one liquidation in a hundred trades puts the 1st percentile at -100%). v2 bounds the tail by the 5th percentile of trade returns (>= -50%) and the liquidated share (<= 2%). Stated here before any v2 number exists
changes_from_v1.everything_else: as v1: markets, panel, costs, carry, plans, periods, harness, baselines, the per-year rule, the hit-rate rule, the selection rule and the validation design

builds_on: research/E4/protocol.json (KOD-GLOBAL-E4-v1) for every field not restated here

CRYPTO.precondition_note: the same panel as v1; v1's precondition (REPRODUCED) stands

US.status: second market, as in v1; the archived inputs are fetched and verified, the repair panel not yet rebuilt

detectors.source: idxsig/rules/moonshot_e4.py: the v1 four (E2 family code copied verbatim) and their _BEAR variants (bear_regime: BTC close < 50-session mean of BTC closes, sessions <= d)
detectors.harness_rule_ids: E4_CAND_<name>; MOONSHOT_E4_D1 after the freeze, with SELECTED_PROTOCOL = KOD-GLOBAL-E4-v2

plans.count_note: as v1 (6 of 36 rows per detector duplicate the hold-1 fixed rows); 36 x 8 = 288 runs

harness.baselines: matched random shorts and same-session random shorts under the same plan, liquidation and jump rule, 200 draws each

admissible_if: average net return > 0 (after fees, slippage, carry and liquidations)
one-sided p < max_p_one_sided_vs_matched against matched random shorts (200 draws; floor 0.005)
average net return > 0 in every discovery calendar year with at least min_scored_per_year scored trades
5th percentile of trade net returns >= max_p5_loss
share of scored trades liquidated <= max_share_liquidated
selection.select: the admissible pair with the highest average net return; ties by more scored trades, then grid order; none admissible = no pair
selection.freeze: the selected tuple is written into idxsig/rules/moonshot_e4.SELECTED with SELECTED_PROTOCOL = KOD-GLOBAL-E4-v2 and committed before any validation statistic

validation.on: validation only, one recorded harness run of MOONSHOT_E4_D1 per market
pass_if: one-sided p < max_p_one_sided_vs_matched against matched random shorts
5th percentile of trade net returns >= max_p5_loss
validation.regime_note: a _BEAR detector fires only in bear sessions; 2023 had few, so min_scored may fail for the right reason, and that is a fail
validation.consequence_if_passed: as v1: a paper policy version may underwrite paper SHORT ON TRIGGER decisions for the pair, scored prospectively; no real orders
validation.consequence_if_failed: no paper policy change; the short-side plan family, with and without the regime condition, is exhausted for these detectors in that market

claims: Historical research, designed on discovery after reading v1's discovery table, tested once on validation if anything is admissible. A pass is one year under assumed costs, carry, liquidation and daily-bar fills. Nothing here is prospective performance, entry permission, or a promise of reliability.
